input_signals.name: Earned Versus Contributed Book Value
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(re, ceq), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Book-to-market only identifies mispricing when the book value was earned rather than raised: a cheap firm whose equity is mostly accumulated retained earnings has demonstrated cash-generating capacity, while a cheap firm whose equity is mostly contributed capital has funded past losses with issuance and its book value carries no evidence of profitability.
input_signals.reasoning: The conditioner is the composition of book equity, not a leverage or solvency ratio, so it avoids the mechanical channel where debt inflates book-to-market and the sort degenerates into a leverage sort — the flaw in both the net-cash version and the earlier weakest-link screen. It also differs from the failed re/at screen because the scaling is by book equity, making it a capital-origin mix that is independent of asset size and of the value leg's own denominator.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( re, ceq ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Unit Cost Stability Within Cheap Firms
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), NEG(ZSCORE(WINSOR(VOL(RATIO(cogs, sale), 5), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap firms with stable cost of goods per dollar of sales operate a controllable production process whose depressed multiple is more likely to be sentiment-driven, whereas cheap firms whose unit costs swing widely face input-price or scale instability that makes future earnings genuinely unforecastable and the discount warranted.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive's only volatility test compared earnings versus cash-flow variability, an accrual-smoothing concept that failed; unit-cost variability is instead a real operating-process attribute measured entirely above the accrual line, so it tests the stability channel where it has economic content rather than accounting content. It also complements the depreciation and asset-composition channels by describing the income statement's input side, keeping the batch's mechanisms non-overlapping.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), neg( zscore( winsor( vol( ratio( cogs, sale ), 5 ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Standardized Depreciation Cut
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)), VOL(RATIO(dp, at), 5)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: What signals accounting discretion is not the size of a change in depreciation intensity but its size relative to how much that firm's depreciation intensity normally moves; a one-point drop is meaningful for a firm with a stable charge and meaningless for a firm with a lumpy asset base.
input_signals.reasoning: The raw deviation is dominated cross-sectionally by capital-intensity heterogeneity, so standardizing by the firm's own five-year volatility of dp/at converts it into a firm-specific surprise measure that should be far cleaner in the middle of the distribution — precisely where the current family's Fama-MacBeth slope is weak. This is a measurement refinement to the archive's best-performing mechanism rather than a new channel, appropriate now that the mechanism is established.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( ratio( dp, at ), ma( ratio( dp, at ), 3 ) ), vol( ratio( dp, at ), 5 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Downside Only Depreciation Discretion
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)), ABS(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The information in depreciation policy is one-sided: cutting the charge below the firm's own norm inflates earnings and marks a trap, whereas charging more than the norm is ordinary asset renewal or conservatism that carries no additional good news.
input_signals.reasoning: The construction SUB(x, ABS(x)) is exactly twice the negative part of the deviation, so all firms at or above their norm are pooled and only the cutters are ordered, which tests whether the family's alpha comes from shorting earnings-inflating traps or from a symmetric spread. Knowing which side carries the payoff determines whether future refinements should target trap identification or bargain identification, and an asymmetric signal that concentrates the short leg may raise both alpha and its t-stat.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), zscore( winsor( sub( sub( ratio( dp, at ), ma( ratio( dp, at ), 3 ) ), abs( sub( ratio( dp, at ), ma( ratio( dp, at ), 3 ) ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Normalized Depreciation Earnings Yield
input_signals.expression: RATIO(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), MUL(at, MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3))), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
input_signals.hypothesis: Restating earnings with the depreciation charge the firm would have taken at its own three-year average intensity strips out the discretionary component of the charge, so the resulting yield ranks firms by cheapness on capital-consumption-honest earnings rather than on reported earnings.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the additive rank stack — which the critic correctly noted would have its slope dominated by the earnings-yield leg and could not distinguish separability from value rediscovery — with a single continuous multiple in which the quality adjustment lives inside the numerator, so a firm cheap only because it under-depreciated is mechanically demoted rather than merely down-weighted. Because the output is a smooth yield rather than a skewed rank product, it is the natural candidate to fix the family's weak Fama-MacBeth slope while preserving the depreciation-discretion mechanism that generates the alpha.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( sub( add( ib, dp ), mul( at, ma( ratio( dp, at ), 3 ) ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) )

input_signals.name: Depreciation Rate On Long Lived Assets
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(dp, SUB(at, act)), MA(RATIO(dp, SUB(at, act)), 3)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Depreciation is charged against long-lived assets only, so the economically correct discretion measure is the charge per dollar of non-current assets; scaling by total assets mixes in working-capital-heavy firms whose low dp/at reflects business model rather than policy.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a measurement correction to the archive's best mechanism, not a new channel: the deviation is computed on the actual depreciable base, which should sharpen the conditioner most for firms whose current-asset share is changing and reduce the cross-sectional noise that has kept the family's Fama-MacBeth slopes near 1.7. It also inherits the gen-2 finding that the interaction is not mechanical, since the EBITDA-yield leg contains no depreciation term.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), zscore( winsor( sub( ratio( dp, sub( at, act ) ), ma( ratio( dp, sub( at, act ) ), 3 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Chronic Depreciation Conservatism Count
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)), 0), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: What distinguishes an honest reporter from an opportunistic one is not the size of a single year's deviation but how habitually the firm charges above its own norm; a cheap firm that has been consistently conservative for several consecutive years has no hidden earnings inflation left to unwind, while a firm that is conservative only occasionally is managing the charge episodically.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a frequency conditioner, not a linear part of the deviation, so it is not implied by decomposing the symmetric and downside results — two firms with identical current deviations receive different scores depending on their record, which is exactly the information a magnitude measure discards. A three-year count keeps the history requirement modest so coverage stays near the family's 0.13, and the discreteness of the count spreads firms across a handful of well-populated groups rather than into thin tails, which is where the family's cross-sectional slope has been leaking.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), zscore( ts_sum( indicator( sub( ratio( dp, at ), ma( ratio( dp, at ), 3 ) ), 0 ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Impairment Exposure Weighted Discretion
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(dp, SUB(at, act)), MA(RATIO(dp, SUB(at, act)), 3)), 1)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(at, act), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Depreciation discretion only matters economically in proportion to how much of the balance sheet is exposed to it: for an asset-heavy cheap firm a shortfall in the charge translates into a large overstatement of both earnings and book value, while for an asset-light firm the same policy deviation is economically trivial.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not a rescaling of the conditioner but an exposure weighting: the non-negative long-lived-asset share amplifies the signed discretion score, so cheap asset-heavy under-depreciators are pushed to the short extreme and cheap asset-heavy conservatives to the long extreme, while asset-light firms are compressed toward neutral regardless of their policy. It converts the conditioner from a uniform-treatment-effect assumption into one where treatment intensity varies with the firm's actual depreciable base, which is the economically correct specification and should sharpen both tails.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), mul( zscore( winsor( sub( ratio( dp, sub( at, act ) ), ma( ratio( dp, sub( at, act ) ), 3 ) ), 1 ) ), rank( ratio( sub( at, act ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Impairment Adjusted Book To Market
input_signals.expression: RATIO(SUB(ceq, TS_SUM(SUB(MUL(at, MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)), dp), 3)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
input_signals.hypothesis: Book equity is overstated by the cumulative amount of depreciation a firm failed to charge relative to its own normal intensity, so writing that shortfall off the book gives a cheapness measure on assets that will survive audit; firms that look cheap only before the adjustment are carrying stale asset values.
input_signals.reasoning: Rather than averaging two highly correlated price multiples, this changes the quantity being priced: the quality adjustment is applied cumulatively to the balance sheet rather than to one year's earnings, which moves firms materially across book-to-market deciles instead of merely reweighting them. The earnings-side embedding produced a strong cross-sectional slope but no alpha because it stayed close to E/P; a book-side embedding tests whether the same discretion information carries portfolio value when it is capitalized over three years into the value anchor itself.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( sub( ceq, ts_sum( sub( mul( at, ma( ratio( dp, at ), 3 ) ), dp ), 3 ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) )

input_signals.name: Magnitude Plus Chronicity Discretion
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ADD(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)), 1)), ZSCORE(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)), 0), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A cheap firm is most credibly mispriced when its depreciation charge is both currently far above its norm and has been above it repeatedly, because a single large deviation can be an asset-mix accident while a persistent pattern reveals a conservative reporting policy.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive has cleanly separated the two statistical roles — magnitude carries the alpha (4.9%, t=4.76, Sharpe 0.51) and chronicity carries the cross-sectional slope (fmb 3.62) — and these are different functions of the same underlying deviation, so summing their standardized versions is a targeted attempt to obtain both forms of evidence rather than a generic composite. Because both legs derive from one economic channel they should reinforce rather than dilute, unlike the earlier composites that mixed accounting policy with balance-sheet liquidity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), add( zscore( winsor( sub( ratio( dp, at ), ma( ratio( dp, at ), 3 ) ), 1 ) ), zscore( ts_sum( indicator( sub( ratio( dp, at ), ma( ratio( dp, at ), 3 ) ), 0 ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Slide From Peak Recognition
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), TS_MAX(RATIO(dp, at), 5)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Under-recognition accumulates gradually, so the informative benchmark is the highest depreciation intensity the firm has ever sustained: a cheap firm still charging near its historical peak has nothing deferred, while one whose charge has drifted far below its own peak has been progressively capitalizing costs that a moving average partially absorbs into the benchmark.
input_signals.reasoning: A three-year moving average is contaminated by the very drift it is meant to detect — a firm that cuts depreciation each year pulls its own benchmark down and looks innocent — whereas a five-year maximum is a ratchet benchmark immune to that contamination. This is a different benchmark concept rather than a rescaling, and because the measure retains magnitude it should preserve the tail behaviour that generates alpha in this family.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), zscore( winsor( sub( ratio( dp, at ), ts_max( ratio( dp, at ), 5 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Recentered Conjunctive Quality Screen
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(MIN(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(che, lct), at), 1)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A cheap firm qualifies as a bargain only if it clears both hurdles — depreciation charged at least in line with its own norm and cash covering near-term obligations — so its quality score should be the weaker of the two conditions, with firms failing either one classified as traps.
input_signals.reasoning: The critic's objection was purely a construction defect: MIN of two un-recentered z-scores has a strongly negative mean, so the product loaded negatively on cheapness for most firms, exactly the flaw behind the archived weakest-link inversion. Wrapping the MIN in an outer ZSCORE restores a zero mean so that roughly half the cross-section receives positive weight on cheapness and half negative, which preserves the intended long leg of cheap-and-doubly-clean firms and short leg of cheap-and-failing firms while keeping the conjunctive economics that distinguishes this test from the archived additive composite.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), zscore( min( zscore( winsor( sub( ratio( dp, at ), ma( ratio( dp, at ), 3 ) ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( che, lct ), at ), 1 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Conjunction With Leverage Not Liquidity
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(MIN(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)), 1)), NEG(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(lt, at), 1))))))
input_signals.hypothesis: If the conjunctive screen works because a cheap firm must clear both an accounting-honesty hurdle and a balance-sheet-survival hurdle, then substituting total-liability burden for cash cover should reproduce the effect; if it works only with cash, the second hurdle is specifically about immediate funding rather than solvency generally.
input_signals.reasoning: This is the decisive content-versus-structure test for the archive's best-performing design: the conjunctive operator and the depreciation leg are held fixed and only the survival condition changes from near-term cash cover to overall leverage. Because leverage-based conditioners have consistently inverted in additive form here, a positive result would demonstrate that the nonlinear weakest-link structure, not the choice of safety variable, is what rescues the interaction.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), zscore( min( zscore( winsor( sub( ratio( dp, at ), ma( ratio( dp, at ), 3 ) ), 1 ) ), neg( zscore( winsor( ratio( lt, at ), 1 ) ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Discrete Two Hurdle Quality Score
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(ADD(INDICATOR(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)), 0), INDICATOR(RATIO(SUB(che, lct), at), 0))))
input_signals.hypothesis: What matters is not how far a cheap firm clears each hurdle but how many hurdles it clears at all: passing both the depreciation-honesty and cash-cover tests is the qualitative distinction between quality value and a value trap.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive shows magnitude carries alpha through fat tails while ordinal measures carry the slope, so a discrete zero-one-two score is the extreme ordinal case — it pools firms into three well-populated groups, which should produce a stable Fama-MacBeth slope and portfolio legs that do not rotate on outliers. It also implements the same two economic conditions as the conjunctive screen but with an additive-in-counts rather than weakest-link aggregation, isolating whether the nonlinearity or the discreteness is what helps.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), zscore( add( indicator( sub( ratio( dp, at ), ma( ratio( dp, at ), 3 ) ), 0 ), indicator( ratio( sub( che, lct ), at ), 0 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Three Source Weakest Link Screen
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(MIN(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)), 1)), MIN(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(che, lct), at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dp), lt), 1))))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A cheap firm survives the trap classification only if it clears three hurdles drawn from three different statements — honest depreciation recognition on the income statement, cash covering near-term obligations on the balance sheet, and maintenance-adjusted operating cash flow covering total liabilities on the cash-flow statement — and failing the weakest of these is what defines a value trap.
input_signals.reasoning: The critic correctly noted that a chronicity count built from the same dp/at deviation is a correlated relabelling rather than an independent hurdle, so the third condition is replaced by debt-service capacity measured from cash flow, which shares no input with either existing leg. Each hurdle now comes from a distinct financial statement, so the MIN genuinely binds on different firms for different reasons, which is the condition under which a weakest-link aggregation can add information rather than noise.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), zscore( min( zscore( winsor( sub( ratio( dp, at ), ma( ratio( dp, at ), 3 ) ), 1 ) ), min( zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( che, lct ), at ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( oancf, dp ), lt ), 1 ) ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Enterprise Anchored Hurdle Count
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)))), ZSCORE(ADD(INDICATOR(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)), 0), INDICATOR(RATIO(SUB(che, lct), at), 0))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheapness of the operating business, measured against the whole capital structure rather than equity alone, is the anchor on which the quality hurdles should operate, because leveraged equity looks cheap for financing reasons that the hurdles are not designed to detect.
input_signals.reasoning: The stock-anchor test failed dramatically (book-to-market flipped the conjunctive alpha from +4.8% to -2.1%) while operating anchors succeeded, and enterprise value is the purest operating anchor available since it removes the mechanical leverage inflation that contaminates equity multiples. Its earlier pairing with an asset-composition conditioner produced 4.3% alpha, so testing it with the archive's strongest conditioner design determines whether the leading result can be improved by cleaning the value leg rather than the quality leg.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sub( add( dltt, dlc ), che ) ) ) ), zscore( add( indicator( sub( ratio( dp, at ), ma( ratio( dp, at ), 3 ) ), 0 ), indicator( ratio( sub( che, lct ), at ), 0 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Sales Anchored Hurdle Count
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(ADD(INDICATOR(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)), 0), INDICATOR(RATIO(SUB(che, lct), at), 0))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Revenue-based cheapness identifies firms the market has written off at the top line, including loss-makers that earnings-based multiples cannot rank, and the two clean-bill hurdles separate those with recoverable franchises from those in terminal decline.
input_signals.reasoning: Anchor choice has proven to be the single largest driver of sign in this archive — operating anchors work and the balance-sheet anchor inverts — so the final anchor question is whether the effect strengthens as the anchor moves further up the income statement, where accounting discretion has least influence on the multiple itself. Sales yield previously delivered 4.3% alpha with the continuous conditioner, and pairing it with the superior count design tests the anchor and the aggregation jointly at no cost to coverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sale, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), zscore( add( indicator( sub( ratio( dp, at ), ma( ratio( dp, at ), 3 ) ), 0 ), indicator( ratio( sub( che, lct ), at ), 0 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Industry Neutral Sales Anchor Count
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(ADD(INDICATOR(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)), 0), INDICATOR(RATIO(SUB(che, lct), at), 0))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Sales-to-price is mechanically determined by an industry's margin structure — a distributor and a software firm at identical mispricing have completely different sales yields — so ranking revenue cheapness within industry isolates genuine write-downs rather than sorting on where a firm sits in the value chain.
input_signals.reasoning: Industry neutralization was tested only on the EBITDA anchor, where margins differ far less across sectors and it cut alpha from 4.9% to 3.1%; for the sales anchor the confound it removes is first-order rather than second-order, so the same operator has a different expected effect and the test is not a repeat. The archive's sales-anchored count already achieves the best joint evidence, and its main weakness is a modest 0.28 Sharpe consistent with a persistent sector tilt.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( sale, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), zscore( add( indicator( sub( ratio( dp, at ), ma( ratio( dp, at ), 3 ) ), 0 ), indicator( ratio( sub( che, lct ), at ), 0 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Enterprise Anchor With Floored Denominator
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MAX(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), ZSCORE(ADD(INDICATOR(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)), 0), INDICATOR(RATIO(SUB(che, lct), at), 0))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Enterprise cheapness is the right anchor for an operating-quality screen, but the enterprise value of a net-cash firm must not be allowed to collapse toward zero or turn negative, so it should be floored at market capitalization — a firm cannot be cheaper than its equity price implies simply because it holds cash.
input_signals.reasoning: The EV-anchored count produced the archive's largest alpha (6.2%, t=5.08) but the critic correctly identified that the denominator degenerates precisely for the cash-rich firms the liquidity hurdle rewards, so the extreme ranks may be an artifact rather than an economic signal. Flooring the denominator keeps the capital-structure neutrality that motivated the anchor while removing the degenerate region, which should preserve the alpha and clean up the cross-sectional slope.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ebitda, max( add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sub( add( dltt, dlc ), che ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ) ), zscore( add( indicator( sub( ratio( dp, at ), ma( ratio( dp, at ), 3 ) ), 0 ), indicator( ratio( sub( che, lct ), at ), 0 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Gross Profit Anchored Hurdle Count
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ZSCORE(ADD(INDICATOR(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)), 0), INDICATOR(RATIO(SUB(che, lct), at), 0))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The right anchor for an accounting-quality screen is cheapness measured on the income line that management can least manipulate: gross profit sits above depreciation, overhead allocation and provisioning, so a low price per dollar of gross profit is a write-down of the underlying business rather than of a reported number.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the mechanical blend of two correlated anchors with a genuinely new anchor that sits economically between the two best performers — sales yield is too crude because it ignores whether revenue is profitable, EBITDA yield already absorbs overhead policy — and it is the anchor most complementary to a depreciation-discretion hurdle, since the two use non-overlapping parts of the income statement. Gross profit is also defined for firms with negative EBITDA, so the usable cross-section stays as wide as the sales-anchored version that currently produces the archive's best joint evidence.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), zscore( add( indicator( sub( ratio( dp, at ), ma( ratio( dp, at ), 3 ) ), 0 ), indicator( ratio( sub( che, lct ), at ), 0 ) ) ) )
